claims: Muslim holidays are based on the lunar Hijri calendar.
Muslim holidays fall about 11 days earlier each Gregorian year.
The two major, officially observed holidays are Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.
Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan fasting.
Eid al-Adha celebrates sacrifice.
Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha both involve special prayers, charity, and community.
Ramadan is the 9th month of the Islamic year.
Muslims fast from dawn to sunset during Ramadan.
Eid al-Fitr is a 1–3 day celebration at the end of Ramadan.
Eid al-Fitr occurs around March 19-20, 2026.
Eid al-Adha is a 3–4 day festival occurring during the Hajj pilgrimage.
Eid al-Adha occurs around May 26-27, 2026.
Eid al-Adha commemorates Abraham’s obedience.
Al-Hijra is the Islamic New Year.
Al-Hijra is the first day of the month of Muharram.
Mawlid an-Nabi (Milad un Nabi) is a celebration of the birth of the Prophet Muhammad.
Ashura is a day of fasting.
Ashura is significant for both Sunni and Shia Muslims.
Ashura commemorates the liberation from oppression or the martyrdom of Hussein.
Muslim holiday dates are confirmed by the sighting of the new moon.
Moon sighting may cause regional variations.
Common practices on Muslim holidays include attending morning prayers, wearing new clothes, visiting family, charity (Zakat al-Fitr), and sharing meals.
"Eid Mubarak" is the traditional greeting, meaning "Blessed Eid" or "Happy Eid".
Projected dates for Ramadan 2026 are Feb 18 – March 19, 2026.
Projected dates for Eid al-Fitr 2026 are March 19 – March 20, 2026.
Projected dates for Eid al-Adha 2026 are May 26 – May 27, 2026.
Projected dates for Ramadan 2027 are Feb 8 – March 9, 2027.
Projected dates for Eid al-Fitr 2027 are March 9 – March 10, 2027.
